ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r3.claim: The phrase about what God created in their spouses points to the permissibility of women within its proper bounds; min may explain mā or mean the sexual organ, with ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r3.anchor: ما خلق لكم ربكم: يدل على الإباحة بشرطها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r4.claim: If mā means the created organ rather than women, an omitted noun is required for their abandoning intercourse with the created spouses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r4.anchor: ومن إما للتبيين لقوله: ما خلق، وإما للتبعيض: أي العضو المخلوق للوطء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r5.claim: Bal antum qawm ʿādūn transitions to a further charge of exceeding limits; the address pronoun emphasizes that they alone are notorious for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r5.anchor: بل أنتم قوم عادون: أي متجاوزون الحد في الظلم

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r2.claim: “From your wives” may explain what God created or be partitive; on the latter reading, “what He created” means the lawful part of women, and they may have done this with their wives too.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r2.anchor: فيصلح أن يكون تبيينا لما خلق وأن يكون للتبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r3.claim: An ʿādī is one who transgresses through injustice.

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r4.claim: The phrase may mean that, in addition to this grave sin, they transgress in all sins, or that this enormity makes them especially deserving of the label transgressors.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r4.anchor: ومعناه أترتكبون هذه المعصية على عظمها بل أنتم قوم عادون في جميع المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r10.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r10.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār argues against determinism: “leaving” presumes ability to do otherwise; what God created would be imposed rather than left; and attributing transgression to people is incoherent if God creates their acts, as calling someone transgressive for their skin color would be.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r10.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار في ( تفسيره )

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r11.claim: Rāzī summarizes the free-will argument: unless people originate their own acts, praise, blame, commands, and prohibitions cannot properly apply to them.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r11.anchor: فنقول حاصل هذه الوجوه يرجع إلى أن العبد لو لم يكن موجدا الأفعال نفسه لما توجه المدح والذم والأمر والنهي عليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r12.claim: Rāzī notes that this story’s wording has a special force for the free-will debate beyond the commands, prohibitions, praise, and blame in the stories of Moses, Abraham, and Noah.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r12.anchor: ولهذه الآية في هذا المعنى خاصية أزيد مما ورد من الأمر والنهي والمدح والذم في قصة موسى عليه السلام وإبراهيم ونوح وسائر القصص

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r13.claim: Rāzī answers that because God knows these acts will occur, their nonoccurrence is impossible: it would turn divine knowledge into ignorance, so commanding people to refrain would demand the impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r13.anchor: أن الله تعالى لما علم وقوع هذه الأشياء فعدمها محال لأن عدمها يستلزم انقلاب العلم جهلا وهو محال

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r14.claim: A choice between two possible acts requires a preponderant motive or will; that originated motive needs a cause, and if the human causes it regress is infinite, while if God causes it the result is compulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r14.anchor: القادر لما كان قادرا على الضدين امتنع أن يترجح أحد المقدورين على الآخر إلا لمرجح وهو الداعي أو الإرادة وذلك المرجح محدث فله مؤثر

RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r15.claim: Rāzī concludes that these two arguments defeat al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār’s case against determinism.
RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r15.anchor: فثبت بهذين البرهانين القاطعين سقوط ما قاله والله أعلم

BURSEVI:v6p219/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p219/r1.claim: Tadharūn means to leave or discard something because one has little regard for it; the verb has no attested perfect form.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r1.anchor: {وتذرون} تتركون يقال : فلان يذر الشيء أي يقذفه لقلة إعداده به ولم يستعمل ماضيه.

BURSEVI:v6p219/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p219/r2.claim: God created wives for enjoyment; min can denote the female kind generally, or partitive reference to the lawful organ, implying that they also practiced anal intercourse with their wives.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r2.anchor: ومن لبيان أن ما أريد به جنس الإناث وللتبعيض إن أريد به العضو المباح منهن وهو القبل

BURSEVI:v6p219/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p219/r3.claim: The partitive reading makes the verse evidence that anal intercourse with wives and enslaved women is forbidden.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r3.anchor: فتكون الآية دليلا على حرمة أدبار الزوجات والمملوكات

BURSEVI:v6p219/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p219/r4.claim: A hadith says that whoever has intercourse with a woman in her anus is disavowed from what was revealed to Muḥammad and will not be looked upon by God.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أتى امرأة في دبرها فهو بريء مما أنزل على محمد ولا ينظر الله إليه"

BURSEVI:v6p219/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r5.speaker: بعض الصحابة
BURSEVI:v6p219/r5.claim: Some Companions declared that the offender had committed disbelief.

BURSEVI:v6p219/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p219/r6.claim: They are people who overstep the limits in all sins, including this one.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r6.anchor: {بل أنتم قوم عادون} متجاوزون الحد في جميع المعاصي وهذا من جملتها

BURSEVI:v6p219/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v6p219/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa rules that male same-sex intercourse warrants discretionary taʿzīr but no fixed ḥadd, contrary to his two disciples.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r7.anchor: في اللوطي فقال أبو حنيفة : يعزر ولا حد عليه خلافا لصاحبيه

BURSEVI:v6p219/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r8.speaker: مالك
BURSEVI:v6p219/r8.claim: Mālik requires stoning for both participants in male same-sex intercourse, whether married or unmarried.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r8.anchor: وقال مالك : يجب على الفاعل والمفعول به الرجم أحصنا أو لم يحصنا

BURSEVI:v6p219/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p219/r9.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد
BURSEVI:v6p219/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad apply the legal rule for fornication to male same-sex intercourse.
BURSEVI:v6p219/r9.anchor: وعند الشافعي وأحمد حكمه حكم الزنى.

STUDYQURAN:26:165/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r1.claim: Some interpret the passage as describing anal intercourse with both men and women.
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r1.anchor: According to some, these verses mean that these people engaged in

STUDYQURAN:26:165/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r2.claim: The context seems to indicate that Lot’s people avoided women.
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r2.anchor: the context would seem to indicate that they avoided women

STUDYQURAN:26:165/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they engaged in this behavior with foreign men.
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r3.anchor: for some this means that they engaged in this behavior with foreign men (Q).

STUDYQURAN:26:165/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:165/r4.claim: The commentary points to parallel discussions of Lot’s people in three other passages.

TAB-FULL:v17p630/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r2.claim: They abandon their wives’ lawful sexual organs, which God created for them.
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r2.anchor: {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} [الشعراء: 166] يقول: وتدعون الذي خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم من فروجهن، فأحله لكم.

TAB-FULL:v17p630/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r3.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has “ما أصلح لكم ربكم” in place of “ما خلق لكم ربكم.”
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r3.anchor: وذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: «وتذرون ما أصلح لكم ربكم من أزواجكم»

TAB-FULL:v17p630/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r4.claim: Mujāhid says they left women’s front openings for men’s and women’s rear openings.
TAB-FULL:v17p630/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} [الشعراء: 166] قال: تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال وأدبار النساء "

TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r1.claim: They transgress by going beyond the sexual relations God permitted to those He prohibited.
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " {بل أنتم قوم عادون} [الشعراء: 166] قال: قوم معتدون "

TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the phrase as “a transgressing people.”
TAB-FULL:v17p630#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " {بل أنتم قوم عادون} [الشعراء: 166] قال: قوم معتدون "

TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.claim: Al-Tabatabai says Lot's preceding argument rests on a demonstrative proof to which the discussion points, also reflected in the parallel wording cited from al-ʿAnkabut.
TABATABAI:26:167-175/r1.anchor: وقد ظهر من جميع ما مر أن كلامه عليه السلام مبني على حجة برهانية أشير إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r1.claim: What God created for them from their spouses refers to their wives' sexual organs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r1.anchor: ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} يعني: فروج نسائهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid paraphrases their conduct as abandoning women's front openings for men's rear openings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r3.claim: They are unjust transgressors who cross from the lawful to the unlawful and obedience to sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p111#2/r3.anchor: بل أنتم قوم عادون} ظالمون معتدون الحلال إلى الحرام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r2.claim: They leave their wives, whom God created for them, without having intercourse with them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r3.claim: They are transgressors who commit the utmost injustice.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r6.claim: Mujāhid takes what they abandon from their spouses as the women’s front openings.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r6.anchor: {إلا على رب العالمين {164} أتأتون الذكران من العالمين {165} وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} [الشعراء: 164-166] أقبال النساء، في تفسير مجاهد،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r7.speaker: أبو مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r7.claim: Ibn Mujāhid transmits his father’s explanation: they leave women’s front openings and have anal intercourse with men.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r7.anchor: وفي تفسير ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه: {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} [الشعراء: 166] ترككم أقبال النساء، وإتيانكم أدبار الرجال.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says what God made for them from their spouses means women’s genitals; the question rebukes them for having done this.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p519/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: {ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} [الشعراء: 166] ما جعل لكم ربكم من فروج نسائكم، وهذا على الاستفهام، أي: قد فعلتم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p520/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p520/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p520/r1.claim: They are transgressors who have gone beyond God’s command.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p520/r1.anchor: {بل أنتم قوم عادون} [الشعراء: 166] مجاوزون لأمر الله.

ELMALILI:26:160-175/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r3.claim: Lūṭ rebukes the men for abandoning the spouses God created for them.
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r3.anchor: bırakıyorsunuz da sizin için yarattığı çiftleri?

ELMALILI:26:160-175/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r4.claim: He calls them a people who have transgressed beyond proper human conduct.
ELMALILI:26:160-175/r4.anchor: Doğrusu siz insanlıktan çıkmış bir kavimsiniz” (166).

BURHAN:v4p257/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p257/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p257/r8.claim: Bal does not retract their same-sex acts or neglect of women; it clarifies their transgression and shifts to naming their further faults.
BURHAN:v4p257/r8.anchor: والمراد تعديد خطاياهم واتصافهم بهذه الصفات وبل لم ينو ما أضافه إليهم من إتيان الذكور والإعراض عن الإناث

BURHAN:v4p257/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.claim: The author rejects al-Basīṭ's and Ibn Mālik's claim that Qur'anic bal only marks transition, since the Qur'an also uses it to retract and correct.
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.anchor: وزعم صاحب البسيط وابن مالك أنها لا تقع في القرآن إلا بهذا المعنى وليست كذلك

BURHAN:v3p23/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p23/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p23/r2.claim: After affirmative speech, bal either retracts a mistaken human statement or moves to what is more apt; in divine speech it refutes human claims or marks a prior matter as past and shifts to what deserves mention.
BURHAN:v3p23/r2.anchor: واعلم أن بل إذا ذكرت بعد كلام موجب فمعناها الإضراب وهو أما أن يقع في كلام الخلق ومعناه إبطال ما سبق

BURHAN:v3p23/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p23/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p23/r4.claim: In Lot's people's reply, bal turns from their pursuing males and abandoning wives to the judgment that they are transgressors.
BURHAN:v3p23/r4.anchor: أضرب بها عن حقيقة إتيانهم الذكور وترك الأزواج

DAMGHANI:v1p162/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r8.claim: خلق can mean made and permitted; the phrase refers to what God made lawful of women's sexual parts.
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r8.anchor: الخامس : خلق أي جعل قوله جلت قدرته في سورة الشعراء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r1.claim: The root can mean bringing something into existence; another explanation specifies creation according to an estimate and ordered arrangement.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r1.anchor: الخلق : الإيجاد والإحداث . [ وقيل ] الخلق : الإيجاد على تقدير وترتيب .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the root meaning is estimation, citing Zuhayr's verse about carrying out what one has planned or fashioned.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : أصل الخلق : التقدير ، قال زهير : - ولأنت تفري ما خلقت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r3.claim: Ibn Faris explains that preparing a hide for a waterskin means measuring it to shape.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r3.anchor: قال ابن فارس : يقال : خلقت الأديم للسقاء : إذا قدرته .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r5.claim: In ordinary usage, the verb for clouds becoming even is اخلولق.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r6.claim: A level trace across the ground is called مخلولق.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r7.claim: A man described as مختلق is fully formed.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r10.claim: In the verse about spouses, خلق means making or appointing them for people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخلق في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r3.claim: Leaving the wives God created explains their blindness and the consequence of this perversion: attraction to women disappears.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r3.anchor: The words “and leave the wives which your Lord has created for you?” is an explanation of this blindness and the essential consequence of this vulgar tendency.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r4.claim: Such people mock the family and turn society into a herd governed by unnatural desires.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r4.anchor: Such people make a complete mockery of the institution of family and the society becomes a herd of animals driven by unnatural desires.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r5.claim: Calling them people who cross limits conveys yearning and sorrow because their wrongdoing exceeds the limits of human nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r5.anchor: The words “in fact, you are a people who have crossed the limits” express yearning and sorrow.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r1.claim: من is explanatory if ما denotes the female sex, yielding omitted terms for intercourse with their vulvas; it is partitive if ما means the lawful part of spouses, requiring one omitted term for intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r1.anchor: للبيان إن أريد بما جنس الاناث ولعل في الكلام حينئذ مضافين محذوفين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud's reading ما أصلح لكم ربكم من أزواجكم supports the partitive analysis of what God made lawful from spouses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r2.anchor: ويؤيد قراءة ابن مسعود ( ماأصلح لكم ربكم من أزواجكم )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r3.claim: The wording may insinuate that they also approached their wives anally, without explicit condemnation, because it is less sinful than intercourse with males.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r3.anchor: ويكون في الكلام على ما قيل تعريض بأنهم كأنوا يأتون نساءهم أيضا في محاشهن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r4.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r4.claim: The established Sunni position forbids anal intercourse with wives and treats it as a major sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r4.anchor: وهو على المشهور عند أهل السنة حرام بل كبيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r5.claim: Another view permits anal intercourse with wives; the author refers readers to his fuller discussion at 2:223.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو مباح وقد تقدم الكلام في ذلك مبسوطا عند الكلام في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r6.claim: An alternative needs no omitted noun: the people are blamed for abandoning and ignoring what God created for them, even before considering intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r6.anchor: وقيل : ليس في الكلام مضاف محذوف أصلا والمراد ذمهم بترك ما خلق لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r7.claim: عادي means one who transgresses through oppression and exceeds a limit; its omitted complement may be general (all sins) or specific (excess in sexual desire).
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r7.anchor: والعادي المتعدي في ظلمه المتجاوز فيه الحد ومتعلقة مقدر وهو اما عام أو خاص

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r8.claim: A further explanation says they exceed the bounds of desire, surpassing other people and even most animals, or transgress by pursuing what was not created for sex and leaving what was.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r8.anchor: أو متجاوزون عن حد الشهوة حيث زدتم على سائر الناس بل أكثر الحيوانات

ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r9.claim: Al-Bahr says placing the pronoun of address first emphasizes their deed and singles them out as a transgressive people unlike others.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p115/r9.anchor: وفي البحر أن تصديرتصدير الجملة بضمير الخطاب تعظيما لفعلهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r5.claim: Mujahid says they left women's sexual organs for men's backsides.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r6.claim: ʿĀdūn means transgressors who pass beyond what is lawful into what is forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r6.anchor: بل أنتم قوم عادون} معتدون، مجاوزون الحلال إلى الحرام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r2.claim: God created spouses for enjoyment; min is explanatory if “spouses” means women generally, or partitive if it means the lawful part of wives, hinting they also did this with wives.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r2.anchor: للبيان إن أريد به جنس الإناث، أو للتبعيض إن أريد به العضو المباح منهن

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r3.claim: They exceed the bounds of desire beyond people and animals, are excessive sinners, or deserve “aggressors” for this crime.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:159-166/r3.anchor: متجاوزون عن حد الشهوة حيث زادوا على سائر الناس بل الحيوانات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r6.claim: The act for which they abandon their wives is intercourse with women; min may explain what was created for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r6.anchor: أي تتركون لهذا الغرض { ما خلق لكم }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r7.claim: He also allows min to be partitive, with the created part in question being the female sexual organ.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مبغضةن ويكون المخلوق كذلك هو القبل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r8.claim: They did not abandon their wives altogether but left them during sex by turning to males; they evade the point by construing leave as total abandonment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r8.anchor: حملا لقوله على الترك أصلا ورأسا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r9.claim: Lot rejects their evasion: they exceed the limit by turning from wives to males, and transgression is already rooted in them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r9.anchor: قال مضربا عن مقالهم هذا المعلوم تقديره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r10.claim: Their transgression is exceeding the limit in evil, a settled trait that keeps them from God's bounds.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r10.anchor: العدوان - الذي هو مجاوزة الحد في الشر - وصف لكم

DURR-FULL:v6p317/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r1.claim: Mujahid says they abandoned vaginal intercourse with women for anal intercourse with men and with women.
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} قال: تركتم اقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال وأدبار النساء

DURR-FULL:v6p317/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r2.claim: Mujahid explains what God created for them as what is suitable for them, meaning the vagina.
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} قال: ما أصلح لكم يعني القبل

DURR-FULL:v6p317/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r3.claim: Ikrima says they left women's vaginas for men's anuses.
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة {وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} يقول: ترك اقبال النساء إلى ادبار الرجال

DURR-FULL:v6p317/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses transgressors as people who exceed bounds.
DURR-FULL:v6p317/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {بل أنتم قوم عادون} قال: متعدون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says they abandoned women's vaginas for men's and women's anuses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من ازواجكم تركتم اقبال النساء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r2.claim: When asked, Mujahid explains what God made suitable from their wives as the front, meaning vaginal intercourse.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2808#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : سالته ، عن قول الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r3.claim: The rebuke addresses pursuing males and leaving lawful wives; it means abandoning wives during the sinful act, not abandoning women altogether.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r3.anchor: ثم وقفهم على معصيتهم البشعة في إتيان الذكران وترك فروج الأزواج والمعنى ويذر ذلك العاصي في حين معصيته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ما أصلح لكم ربكم in place of ما خلق لكم ربكم.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود «ما أصلح لكم ربكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r5.claim: عادون means wrongdoers who transgress a forbidden limit.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ما أصلح لكم ربكم من أزواجكم; al-Zajjāj explains this as referring to the women's sexual organs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج وقرأ ابن مسعود ما أصلح لكم ربكم من أزواجكم يعني به الفروج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid says they abandoned women's sexual openings for men's backsides.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#3/r3.claim: ʿĀdūn means wrongdoers who transgress limits.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r1.claim: When Lūṭ forbade their lewd approach to males and directed them to their wives, they threatened expulsion unless he stopped preaching.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r1.anchor: لما نهاهم نبي الله عن إتيانهم الفواحش، وغشيانهم الذكور، وأرشدهم إلى إتيان نسائهم

JISHUMI:v7p5380/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r6.claim: Yadharu and yadaʿ mean the same thing; their past forms fell out of use because ترك sufficed and Arabic dislikes beginning with wāw.
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r6.anchor: ويذر ويدع بمعني، وأهمل ماضيها؛ للاستغناء عنه ب (ترك)

JISHUMI:v7p5380/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r7.claim: ʿĀdī and muʿtadī both mean one who goes beyond the truth; ʿĀdī may derive from enmity or from swiftly running.
JISHUMI:v7p5380/r7.anchor: والعادي والمعتدي بمعنى، وهو الخارج عن الحق، والعادي من العداوة

MUJAHID:v2p465/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p465/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p465/r1.claim: Mujahid says they turned from women's front openings to men's backs and women's backs.
MUJAHID:v2p465/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم ﴾ يقول تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال وأدبار النساء

MUQATIL:26:160-173/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:160-173/r8.claim: What God created for them in their wives means the women’s sexual organs.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r1.claim: Min can explain the phrase “what your Lord created for you” or indicate a part of it; the intended part is the permitted sexual organ of the women.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r1.anchor: من تبيين لما خلق أو تبعيض والمراد بما خلق العضو المباح منهن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r2.claim: The people practiced this act with their wives as well.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r3.claim: The verse proves that anal intercourse with wives or female slaves is forbidden; Nasafi calls anyone who permits it gravely mistaken.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r3.anchor: وفيه دليل على تحريم ادبار الزوجات والمملوكات ومن أجازه فقد أخطأ خطأ عظيما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r4.claim: ʿĀdī means a transgressor who exceeds the limit in injustice; their grave act makes them especially deserving of that description.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#9/r4.anchor: العادى المتعدى فى ظلمه المتجاوز فيه الحد أى بل أنتم قوم أحق بأن توصوا بالعدوان
